groups.title: Advanced Loader Patterns
groups.question: After every action, Remix refetches data for every route on the page, and a deep component needs the parent's user data. Explain revalidation and accessing parent data.

followUps.Revalidation and shouldRevalidate: Why does Remix revalidate loaders after actions, and when would you skip it?
followUps.useLoaderData vs useRouteLoaderData: How can a deeply nested component use a parent route's data?

evidence.text: By default, all active loaders run again after an action.
This keeps data consistent with the change.
shouldRevalidate lets a route skip refetching when its data cannot have changed.
useRouteLoaderData reads a loader's data by route id.
It avoids passing data through many components.
useLoaderData only returns the current route's own data.

notEnough: Only saying you read loader data.

groups.title: Advanced Prisma Patterns
groups.question: Your activity feed gets slow on later pages, and listing projects with their owners makes many queries. Explain how you would paginate and load relations with Prisma.

followUps.Pagination with cursor-based vs offset: Why is cursor pagination better than skip and take for big tables?
followUps.N+1 Queries and include vs select: How can loading relations cause an N+1 problem, and how do you avoid it?

evidence.text: Skip makes the database read and discard all earlier rows.
Deep pages get slower as the table grows.
A cursor continues from the last item and stays fast.
Querying relations inside a loop runs one query per item.
Loading the relations in the main query avoids that.
Selecting only needed nested fields keeps the result small.

groups.title: Data Validation
groups.question: Your action trusts the shape of form data because TypeScript says so, and form errors are wired up by hand everywhere. Explain how you would validate and build forms.

followUps.Zod for Schema Validation: Why validate with Zod when you already have TypeScript types?
followUps.conform for Type-Safe Forms: What does conform add on top of Zod?

evidence.text: TypeScript types do not exist at runtime.
Zod checks and parses the actual form or JSON data.
Invalid data returns clear errors instead of reaching the database.
conform connects Zod schemas to HTML forms.
It binds errors to fields with accessible attributes.
It works with progressive enhancement, with and without JavaScript.

groups.title: Multi-tenancy Patterns
groups.question: A user can view another company's invoice by changing the id in the URL, and two people editing the same record overwrite each other. Explain how you would prevent both.

followUps.Row-Level Security via Loader Guards: How do you stop users from loading other users' records?
followUps.Optimistic Concurrency with version Fiel: How does a version field prevent lost updates?

evidence.text: Every query for user data is scoped to the logged-in user or tenant.
Fetching by record id alone lets users change the id to see other data.
This check is needed in every loader and action, not just the UI.
Each record has a version number.
Updates include the expected version and increment it.
If no row was updated, someone else changed it first, so the user is told.

notEnough: Only saying you use a version.
